Law: The Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961: Governs marriage, divorce, and related matters for Muslims in Pakistan, including provisions for marriage registration, polygamy restrictions, and divorce procedures.
The Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929: Prohibits child marriages. Sets minimum age for marriage (18 years for males, 16 years for females, though provincial variations exist).
The Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939: Provides grounds for Muslim women to seek divorce, including cruelty, desertion, and failure to maintain.
The Dowry and Bridal Gifts (Restriction) Act, 1976: Restricts the giving and receiving of dowry, though enforcement varies.
The Family Courts Act, 1964: Establishes family courts to handle marriage, divorce, custody, and maintenance cases with simplified procedures.
The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890: Governs guardianship and custody of children, relevant in marriage and divorce contexts.
The West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964: Provides framework for family courts to handle matrimonial disputes.
The Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1962: Applies Islamic personal law to Muslims in matters of marriage, divorce, and inheritance.
The Registration of Marriages Act (various provinces): Requires registration of marriages, though implementation varies by province.
The Prevention of Anti-Women Practices (Criminal Law Amendment) Act, 2011: Criminalizes forced marriages and other harmful practices related to marriage.
The Punjab Marriage Restraint (Amendment) Act, 2015: Sets minimum marriage age and requires marriage registration in Punjab.
The Sindh Child Marriage Restraint Act, 2013: Prohibits child marriage in Sindh province, setting minimum age requirements.
The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Child Marriage Restraint Act, 2014: Prohibits child marriage in KPK province.
The Balochistan Child Marriage Restraint Act, 2014: Prohibits child marriage in Balochistan province.
The Hindu Marriage Act, 2017: Governs marriage and divorce for Hindus in Pakistan.
The Christian Marriage Act, 1872: Governs marriage ceremonies and registration for Christians in Pakistan.
The Special Marriage Act, 1872: Provides for civil marriages for people of different religions or those who prefer civil ceremonies.
The Maintenance of Wives and Children Act, 1958: Provides for maintenance (nafaqa) for wives and children after divorce or separation.
The Muslim Family Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1961: Contains provisions regarding polygamy, requiring permission from Arbitration Council and existing wife's consent.
The Protection of Women (Criminal Laws Amendment) Act, 2006: Includes provisions related to marital rape and domestic violence within marriage.
